title: Digital modes, bandwidth and constellations
blurb: How QAM and constellation diagrams work, how symbol rate relates to data rate, and how bandwidth and error correction behave.

E8C01.why: QAM modulates the **amplitude of two same-frequency carriers 90° apart**, giving many phase and amplitude states.
E8C01.trap: It is not a compression or analog TV technique.

E8C02.why: A symbol is one state of the waveform. Symbol rate is **how fast the waveform changes** to convey information.
E8C02.trap: Characters per second is a data rate, not a symbol rate.

E8C03.why: A phase change at a zero crossing avoids a sudden jump in the wave, which **minimizes bandwidth**.

E8C04.why: **Sinusoidal data pulses** change smoothly, so PSK31 stays narrow. Linear pulses have sharper corners.

E8C05.why: A CW signal's bandwidth is roughly 4 × its speed in WPM: 13 × 4 = **52 Hz**.

E8C06.why: An FT8 signal is **50 Hz** wide, narrower than an SSB voice signal.
E8C06.trap: 2.4 kHz is a typical voice bandwidth, not FT8.

E8C07.why: FSK bandwidth ≈ baud + 1.2 × shift: 9.6 kHz + 1.2 × 4.8 kHz = **15.36 kHz**.
E8C07.trap: 5.76 kHz is only the 1.2 × shift part.

E8C08.why: ARQ detects an error and **requests a retransmission**. It does not correct bits itself.
E8C08.trap: Codes that correct errors automatically are forward error correction.

E8C09.why: **Gray code** changes exactly one bit between consecutive values: 00, 01, 11, 10.
E8C09.trap: BCD, EBCDIC and ASCII are character codes without that property.

E8C10.why: Rate = symbol rate × bits per symbol, so a **more efficient code** sends more bits in the same bandwidth.
E8C10.trap: Forward error correction adds redundant bits, which lowers net data rate.

E8C11.why: Baud counts waveform changes per second, which is the **symbol rate**. They are the same number.
E8C11.trap: Bit rate is what differs: it is baud times bits per symbol.

E8C12.why: A CW signal widens with faster **keying speed** and with sharper **rise and fall times** (shape factor).
E8C12.trap: Modulation index and IF bandwidth do not set a transmitted CW signal's width.

E8C13.why: Each dot in the diagram is an allowed symbol: the **possible phase and amplitude states** for each symbol.
E8C13.trap: It does not show frequency response or error-correction bits.

E8C14.why: Mesh nodes use **Internet Protocol (IP) addresses**, like any network.

E8C15.why: Nodes find neighbours and build the mesh with **discovery and link establishment protocols**.
